pr_title: Add support for reindex over CCS
pr_comment: Hi @volodk85, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Thank you @DaveCTurner for having a look.

I added `ignore_unavailable` to Reindex API query parameters. Now in order to use reindex from remote, users have to specify it explicitly. `ignore_unavailable` index option does not depend on `skip_unavailable` remote cluster setting.
```
curl -X POST "localhost:19200/_reindex?ignore_unavailable=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d'
{
  "source": {
    "index": "cluster0:my-index-000001"
  },
  "dest": {
    "index": "my-index-000001"
  }
}
```

With this change Reindex API behaves as follow (assuming remote index does not exists):
`ignore_unavailable`: **true**
Local -> Local: Call successful 
Remote -> Local: Call sucessful
both report zeros in total/create/update/delete metrics
```
{"took":24,"timed_out":false,"total":0,"updated":0,"created":0,"deleted":0,"batches":0,"version_conflicts":0,"noops":0,"retries":{"bulk":0,"search":0},"throttled_millis":0,"requests_per_second":-1.0,"throttled_until_millis":0,"failures":[]}
```
`ignore_unavailable`: **false**
Local -> Local: Operation fails (index not found)
Remote -> Local: Operation fails due to gating in [IndexNameExpressionResolver.java](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2e6834ad1103f7eab2e5a9cf2dcb5816ec4d2d17/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/IndexNameExpressionResolver.java#L1612-L1622) **Call to remote does not happen at all!**

>Often folks will want the reindex to fail if the source index is unavailable, but with this option I think it'll report success without having copied everything over

I agree that API should behave in the same way regardless we query local or remote index - if it does not exist, there should be clear error statement.

Now I wonder why the condition which mandates presence of `ignore_unavailable` flag for querying remote index in [IndexNameExpressionResolver.java](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2e6834ad1103f7eab2e5a9cf2dcb5816ec4d2d17/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/IndexNameExpressionResolver.java#L1612-L1622) was ever introduced?
If it only for fixing datemath expression as commit message suggest (Fix indices resolver for datemath with colon  (#92973) Albert Zaharovits* 2023-01-18, 9:41 a.m.) IMHO it sounds like using wrong tool to solve the problem. Currently reindex API requires to slap `ignore_unavailable` flag for ability to "touch" remote index regardless its availability/existence of other side of wire. This contradicts with CCS api which allows to query remote index without having those query param. Taking into account that CCR and CCS are closely related, I expect they behave in the same way when it comes to query remotes.

@albertzaharovits could you please comment?

The core change here is to stop evaluating remote expressions on local node. If the expression is remote, it will be evaluated on remote node when request reaches target node. By doing this, it is possible to lift current restriction of having `ignore_unvailable` flag whenever we try to _reindex from remote.

Could we try the approach [mentioned in my comment on the issue](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/89120#issuecomment-1205256149) and just skip remote indices when validating the reindex request? In other words, adjust `org.elasticsearch.reindex.ReindexValidator#validateAgainstAliases` rather than the `IndexNameExpressionResolver` itself? We're only trying to avoid reindexing with the same source and target, but remote indices cannot be a target in any case so there's no need to resolve them here.

Recap of changes in this PR
1. `IndexNameExpressionResolver ` is not touched
2. reindex api now respects `ignore_unavailable` request option which is propagated in underlying search request
3. Fix for datemath expression: remote name with complex datemath expressions containing `:` symbol was treated as a "remote-of-remote" names.

Noteworthy that in current `main` it is not possible to `_search/_count` from index which name is represented by a valid but rather complex datemath expression e.g. <datemath-{2001-01-01-13||+1h/h{yyyy-MM-dd-HH|-07:00}}> 

Before fix
```
curl -X GET "localhost:9200/%3Cdatemath-%7B2001-01-01-13%7C%7C%2B1h%2Fh%7Byyyy-MM-dd-HH%7C-07%3A00%7D%7D%3E/_count"
{"error":{"root_cause":[{"type":"no_such_remote_cluster_exception","reason":"no such remote cluster: [<datemath-{2001-01-01-13||+1h/h{yyyy-MM-dd-HH|-07]"}],"type":"no_such_remote_cluster_exception","reason":"no such remote cluster: [<datemath-{2001-01-01-13||+1h/h{yyyy-MM-dd-HH|-07]"},"status":404}
```
After fix
```
curl -X GET "localhost:9200/%3Cdatemath-%7B2001-01-01-13%7C%7C%2B1h%2Fh%7Byyyy-MM-dd-HH%7C-07%3A00%7D%7D%3E/_count"
{"count":100,"_shards":{"total":1,"successful":1,"skipped":0,"failed":0}}% 
```
